title: Ramayana Opens With Rs 42.96 Crore in Day 1 Advance Sales, Bollywood's Second-Best Ever
excerpt: 12.14 lakh tickets sold before the first show, a record 26,615 shows, and the highest pre-sales ever for a non-sequel — the Ranbir Kapoor-Yash epic starts its run in the record books.
body:
• Ramayana closed its day 1 advance booking at Rs 42.96 crore gross in India excluding blocked seats — Rs 50.08 crore including them — from 12.14 lakh tickets, per Sacnilk figures reported by Koimoi and The Hollywood Reporter India.
  • That makes it Bollywood's second-best opening-day pre-sales ever, behind only Dhurandhar 2 (Rs 53 crore) and ahead of Jawan (Rs 40.75 crore) — and the highest ever for a non-sequel.
  • The film opened across 26,615 shows, the highest show count ever for a Bollywood film, in Hindi, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam versions.
  • Koimoi projects an opening day of Rs 91-101 crore net in India; Sacnilk's live day 1 tracking will confirm the trajectory through Thursday.

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, arrived in theatres on Thursday with the kind of advance booking Bollywood measures records by. As per the final day 1 advance booking update reported by Koimoi, the film sold 12.14 lakh tickets before its first show and grossed Rs 42.96 crore through opening-day pre-sales in India, equal to Rs 36.41 crore net. Including blocked seats, the final tally was Rs 50.08 crore gross from 14.05 lakh tickets, according to trade tracker Sacnilk figures reported by The Hollywood Reporter India.

Where it sits in the record book

On the like-for-like measure — gross pre-sales excluding blocked seats — Ramayana's Rs 42.96 crore is Bollywood's second-best opening-day advance ever, surpassing Jawan's Rs 40.75 crore and standing behind only Dhurandhar 2 at Rs 53 crore. Animal (Rs 33.97 crore) and Pathaan (Rs 32.01 crore) complete the top five. As a non-sequel — a first film, not a franchise continuation — its pre-sales are the highest ever recorded. The film, produced by Namit Malhotra and released in Hindi with Kannada, Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam versions, is the first part of a planned two-part epic; Part 2 is confirmed for Diwali 2028.

The language split and the show count

Of the Rs 42.96 crore, the original Hindi version contributed Rs 31.68 crore, followed by Kannada at Rs 4.95 crore, Telugu at Rs 4.08 crore, Tamil at Rs 1.53 crore and Malayalam at Rs 71.79 lakh, Koimoi reported. The film secured 26,615 shows across India — the highest show count ever for a Bollywood film, and second among Indian films only to Pushpa 2's 32,140. That show count matters in a pre-Diwali week: even at decent occupancy, the sheer number of screenings offsets the traditionally soft festive-period footfall.

What opening day could deliver

Koimoi projects a first day of Rs 91-101 crore net at the Indian box office, with the Hindi version alone likely to contribute Rs 68-74 crore net — which would make it Bollywood's second-biggest opening after Dhurandhar 2's Rs 145 crore net. The Hollywood Reporter India, citing Sacnilk, reported international pre-sales had crossed Rs 111 crore a day before release and projected a worldwide day 1 gross above Rs 150 crore. The advance campaign began on October 20, more than two weeks before release, and built steadily rather than spiking on star-driven opening-day demand — the pattern trade trackers associate with family audiences booking for the Diwali weekend ahead.
